newsitem.title: USA: Most US stock index futures end up, S&P recovers.
newsitem.headline: Most US stock index futures end up, S&P recovers.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures ended mostly higher in a session that featured a dramatic Standard and Poor's 500 futures recovery.
Stock indices collapsed in early pit trading, focusing on news before the opening that Intel Corp had warned its second-quarter revenue and profit would fall short of expectations.
Nasdaq led the declines and June S&P 500s tumbled as much as 14.00 points in heavy trading.
But June S&P 500s did not fall the full 15-point intitial trading limit as many had expected, and soon recovered.

June rallied into the close, charging almost to the 854.70 all-time high set earlier this week. Traders cited a firm Treasury bond futures close and technical optimism after June S&Ps weathered the barrage of early selling so well.

Analysts said June S&P 500s showed typical resilience. "By breaking down through support and now reversing itself it's a pretty good indication of the market," said Jay Hohmann, head futures trader with DLJ Securities in New York.
He said the early Intel-sparked selloff presented a "fire sale scenario" that bulls and bargain hunters used as a buying opportunity.
David Hightower, an analyst with The Hightower Report in Chicago, said June posted a classic bottom-type pattern Friday.
"When you spike down and then you recover above mid-range, that really finishes off the bottoming action," Hightower said.
June S&P 500 futures built on that technical formation to extend the rally into the close, traders said.
They noted, however, that the market was choppy at the day's highs and ran out of steam before retesting the record high set Tuesday.
However, June Russell 2000, NYSE Composites and KCBT Value Line indicies all hit fresh record highs.

At the close, June S&P 500s were up 5.10 points at 850.60, Nasdaq 100 was off 10.90 points at 962.75, NYSE Composites were up 3.45 at 442.80, KCBT Value Lines rose 3.95 to 755.80, Nikkeis were down 160 at 20,140, Midcap 400s were up 2.80 at 279.65, and Russell 2000s were up 1.90 at 380.60.
